newsitem.title: CHINA: Senior U.S. official in talks on China summit.
newsitem.headline: Senior U.S. official in talks on China summit.

text.p: U.S. National Security Adviser Sandy Berger began meetings on Monday with Chinese officials in talks expected to focus on an upcoming summit between the presidents of the Pacific rim giants.
Berger began talks in Beijing with Liu Huaqiu, director of the Foreign Affairs Office under China's State Council, or cabinet, at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse, a Foreign Ministry official said.
The talks were due to continue throughout the day, the official said.

Berger, who arrived on Sunday, was expected to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Tuesday in the seaside resort of Beidaihe where China's leaders are gathered to decide policy and personnel changes for the next five years.
U.S. officials declined to give details of Berger's talks. Berger is due to leave China on Wednesday.
In Washington, officials said the main goal of his trip was to discuss preparations for Jiang's state visit to the United States planned for late October.

That summit is expected to set the seal on a strengthening in long-fraught Sino-U.S. ties, battered in recent years by disputes ranging from trade and human rights to nuclear proliferation and Taiwan.

Jiang's meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton will be the first state visit to the United States by a Chinese president since China's leaders used the army to crush student-led pro-democracy demonstrations in Beijing's Tiananmen Square on June 3-4, 1989.

Jiang stressed on Sunday the importance of Sino-U.S. ties, saying he wanted to see China and the United States seize on a recent improvement in their rocky relationship as a foundation for healthy long-term contacts.

"This year, Sino-U.S. relations have maintained a steady trend of improvement and developing...contacts between the two countries in various arenas have continued to expand," Jiang said in a meeting with U.S. Republican Senator Strom Thurmond.
"One can say that the United States and China now face a good opportunity for improving and developing relations," Jiang said, referring to hard-won improvements in recent months.

However, Jiang told his staunchly pro-Taiwan guest that continued improvement in Sino-U.S. ties could only come as long as Washington did not waver in its recognition of Beijing as the sole government of China.

"China is willing to work with the United States to take advantage of this timely opportunity and to work on the basis of the three joint communiqus...to develop long-term, stable healthy relations as we face a new age," Jiang said.
Under the three communiqus, the United States switched recognition to China from Taiwan and recognised Beijing's sovereignty over the island.

Washington has shown a commitment to boost ties with China, although Beijing has pounced on more conservative views in the United States that advocate containment over engagement as evidence of U.S. suspicion of Asia's strongest communist state.
